change_class_rationale: Modifies a kernel-class function (oya-check-adr-citation#adr_citations) that participates in admission-gate validation. Behavior change is observable to other consumers; +2 unit tests + 1 production-data restoration validate end-to-end.
task: Resolve F-ADR-CITATION-KERNEL-BOMINAL-PREFIX-AWARE (filed same-session in PR #56): teach oya-check-adr-citation#adr_citations() to recognize the `Bominal-` namespace prefix so Bominal-ADR-NNNN citations are no longer byte-scanned as local ADR-NNNN. Pre-fix: Bominal-ADR-0106 silently passed only because local ADR-0106 happens to exist (false-positive); Bominal-ADR-0133 hard-failed because local ADR-0133 does not exist. Post-fix: all Bominal-ADR-* tokens are recognized as external-namespace and skipped from the citation count entirely.
artifacts_touched: crates/oya-check-adr-citation/src/lib.rs (adr_citations() function: added 4-line `if index >= 8 && &bytes[index - 8..index] == b"Bominal-" { index += 8; continue; }` branch immediately before the digit-validation; +2 unit tests skips_bominal_namespace_adr_citations + bominal_prefix_does_not_byte_collide_with_local_adr)

docs/decisions/ADR-0122-ontology-crate-rename-from-object-graph.md (line 9: Bominal-ADR-0133 citation restored — production-data validation that the kernel fix correctly skips the unverifiable Bominal-side citation)

registry/fixuptasks.jsonl (F-ADR-CITATION-KERNEL-BOMINAL-PREFIX-AWARE flipped to completed-same-session-2026-05-17 with resolution_note documenting the narrower skip-namespace-prefix variant chosen over the stricter allowlist variant)
local_gates: cargo nextest run -p oya-check-adr-citation --all-features: PASS (6/6 — 4 pre-existing + 2 new)
adr-citation gate (full docs/ tree): PASS (723 docs / 7787 citations / 124 allowed ADRs; citation count dropped from 7795 since Bominal-* tokens no longer count as local)

design_decisions.decision: Skip-namespace-prefix variant chosen over allowed_bominal_adrs allowlist variant.
design_decisions.rejected_alternative: Carry an `allowed_bominal_adrs: BTreeSet<String>` alongside `allowed_pack_adrs`; fail closed when a Bominal-ADR-NNNN citation is not in either set.
design_decisions.rationale: The oyatie repo cannot verify Bominal-side ADR existence without cross-repo access (Bominal lives at /Users/jasonlee/bominal/ — outside this workspace's read scope per docs/AGENTS.md§Boundaries). Fail-closed would block all Bominal citations forever — incompatible with the Bominal-inheritance precedence pattern ([[bominal-inheritance-precedence]] memory) which says 'Inherit Bominal ADR decisions 1:1 by default; oyatie session decisions override Bominal; explicit override list captured'. Skip-and-trust matches that precedence: citations are recorded textually for human review but not gate-validated against a remote allowlist this kernel cannot consult.
design_decisions.future_uplift_when: If/when an oyatie-side Bominal-ADR-allowlist snapshot is bundled (e.g., registry/bominal-adr-allowlist.tsv generated from the Bominal repo manifest), the kernel can move from skip-and-trust to validate-against-allowlist with a backwards-compatible signature extension.

findings: Smallest correct fix: 4 lines added to adr_citations(). No new types, no new public API, no signature change. Byte-scan logic now namespace-aware via a single bounded backward look. Production data (ADR-0122 Bominal-ADR-0133) restored as part of the same commit — validates fix on real data, not just unit tests.

Adversarial fixture `bominal_prefix_does_not_byte_collide_with_local_adr` proves the previously-silent false-positive case: `Bominal-ADR-0056` in the same doc as `ADR-0056` — pre-fix kernel counted 2 citations (both passing because ADR-0056 is allowed; one for the wrong reason); post-fix kernel counts only 1 (the bare ADR-0056). The hidden double-count bug is now testable and prevented.
All 6 crate tests pass (4 pre-existing unaffected + 2 new). Gate end-to-end passes on production data. No cargo fmt/clippy issues (verified via cargo check; full fmt/clippy via CI lanes).

No data-class, autonomy-ceiling, or licence surface touched. The kernel still fails closed on unknown LOCAL ADRs (DisallowedAdrCitation for ADR-NNNN outside allowed_pack_adrs); only the explicit `Bominal-` namespace is skipped. Bominal-inheritance trail at ADR-0122 line 9 fully restored with all 3 Bominal-ADR-* citations preserved.

Audit-chain row appended with distinct timestamp_unix + session_id (OP-08). Resolution trail closes the loop: filed in change_id=claude-adr-citation-mvp-glossary-1778983977 (PR #56) → resolved in change_id=claude-adr-citation-bominal-namespace-1778985172 (this PR). citations_checked metric drops from 7795 to 7787 in the report — the 8-citation delta is the count of `Bominal-ADR-*` tokens previously over-counted across the docs/ tree.

architect.rationale: Smallest correct fix; namespace-prefix recognition is the right abstraction for cross-repo ADR citations. Production-data restoration validates the fix end-to-end, not just at unit-test level.

guardrails: Skip-and-trust is correct given the current cross-repo isolation, but loses the ability to detect dangling Bominal references (an ADR cited by name that no longer exists in Bominal). Future uplift documented in design_decisions[0].future_uplift_when.

If other external-namespace prefixes ever land (e.g., `Foundry-ADR-NNNN`, `Workspace-ADR-NNNN`), the current implementation hardcodes only `Bominal-`. A more general approach would table-ize the recognized prefixes. Trivial to add when the second prefix shows up — premature now.
